title.en: Volume 116 Book of Later Zhou 18: Shizong Annals 3
title.raw: 卷一百十六 周書7: 世宗本紀三 Volume 116 Book of Later Zhou 18: Shizong Annals 3

sentences.zh: 顯德三年春正月乙未朔，帝不受朝賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month in spring of the third year of Xiande (day yiwei), the Emperor did not accept court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day in spring of the third year of Xiande, the Emperor declined the usual New Year court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 前司空蘇禹珪卒。

translations.literal: The former Minister of Works Su Yugui died.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yugui, the former Minister of Works, died.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，李穀奏，破淮賊於上窯。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, Li Gu memorialized that the Huainan rebels had been defeated at Shangyao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Li Gu reported a victory over the Huainan rebels at Shangyao.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，發丁夫十萬城京師羅城。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, one hundred thousand corvée laborers were mobilized to build the outer wall of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the court drafted one hundred thousand laborers to fortify the capital's outer ramparts.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔取此月八日幸淮南。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, an edict set the eighth day of this month for an imperial visit to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, an edict scheduled the Emperor's departure for Huainan on the eighth of the month.

sentences.zh: 殿中監馬從赟免所居官，坐幹沒外孫女霍氏之資產，為人所訟故也。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Ma Congyun was removed from office for embezzling the assets of his granddaughter née Huo, because he had been sued by others.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Congyun, Director of the Palace Secretariat, was dismissed after being sued for seizing the property of his granddaughter, the Huo family heiress.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以宣徽南院使向訓為權東京留守，以端明殿學士王樸為副留守。

translations.literal: On day xinchou, the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting Eastern Capital regent, and Hanlin academician Wang Pu was made deputy regent.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Xiang Xun of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat was appointed acting regent of the Eastern Capital, with Wang Pu of the Duanming Hall as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，車駕發京師，丁未，李穀奏，自壽州引軍退守正陽。

translations.literal: On day renyin, the imperial carriage departed the capital. On day dingwei, Li Gu memorialized that he had withdrawn his army from Shouzhou to hold Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the Emperor left the capital. On dingwei, Li Gu reported that he had pulled his forces back from Shouzhou to defend Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，李重進奏，大破淮賊於正陽，斬首二萬餘級，伏屍三十里，臨陣斬賊大將劉彥貞，生擒偏將鹹師朗已下，獲戎甲三十萬副、馬五百匹。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, Li Chongjin memorialized that he had routed the Huainan rebels at Zhengyang, taking more than twenty thousand heads; corpses lay for thirty li; in battle he slew the rebel general Liu Yanzhen and captured alive the deputy generals Xian Shilang and others, seizing three hundred thousand suits of armor and five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Li Chongjin reported a great victory at Zhengyang: over twenty thousand enemy dead, bodies strewn for thirty li along the field. He killed the rebel commander Liu Yanzhen in the fighting, took Deputy General Xian Shilang and others alive, and captured three hundred thousand suits of armor and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 先是，李穀駐軍於壽春城下，以攻其城，既而淮南援軍大至，乃與將佐謀曰：「賊軍舟棹將及正陽，我師無水戰之備，萬一橋梁不守，則大軍隔絕矣，不如全師退守正陽浮橋，以俟鑾輅。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Gu had encamped below Shouchun city to attack it. When large Huainan relief forces arrived, he consulted his officers and said: "The rebel fleet will soon reach Zhengyang. Our army is not prepared for naval combat. If the bridge should not be held, the main force would be cut off. It would be better to withdraw the whole army to defend the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang and await the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Gu had besieged Shouchun. When strong Huainan reinforcements arrived, he told his commanders: "The enemy fleet is nearing Zhengyang, and we are not equipped for river fighting. If the bridge falls, the army will be stranded. We should pull back intact to the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang and wait for the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆以為然，遂燔其糧草而退。

translations.literal: All the generals agreed, and they burned their grain and fodder and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The officers all agreed, so they burned their stores and retreated.

sentences.zh: 軍回之際無復嚴整，公私之間頗多亡失，淮北役夫亦有陷於賊境者。

translations.literal: On the march back discipline was no longer maintained; both public and private property suffered considerable losses, and corvée laborers north of the Huai also fell into enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: The withdrawal was disorderly, with heavy losses of government and private property, and some laborers from north of the Huai were captured behind enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，急詔侍衛都指揮使李重進率師赴之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he urgently ordered the Commander of the Palace Guards Li Chongjin to lead troops there.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the Emperor urgently ordered Li Chongjin, Commander of the Palace Guards, to march to their relief.

sentences.zh: 時淮賊乘李穀退軍之勢，發戰棹數百艘沿淮而上，且張斷橋之勢，彥貞以大軍列陣而進。

translations.literal: At that time the Huainan rebels, taking advantage of Li Gu's withdrawal, sent several hundred warships up the Huai and also deployed to sever the bridge; Liu Yanzhen advanced with a large army in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan rebels exploited Li Gu's retreat, sending hundreds of warships up the Huai while positioning to cut the bridge; Liu Yanzhen advanced with his main force in battle order.

sentences.zh: 李重進既至正陽，聞淮軍在近，率諸將渡橋而進，與賊軍遇，重進等合勢擊之，一鼓而敗之。

translations.literal: When Li Chongjin reached Zhengyang and heard the Huainan army was near, he led his generals across the bridge to advance, met the rebel army, and Li Chongjin and the others combined their strength and attacked; at the first drum they routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin reached Zhengyang, learned the enemy was close, and led his officers across the bridge. They met the rebel force and, joining their strength in one assault, broke them at the first charge.

sentences.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》：世宗親征，行至圉鎮，聞蒨軍卻，意唐兵必追之，遣李重進急趨正陽，曰：「唐兵且至，宜急擊之。」

translations.literal: (From Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang: When Shizong campaigned in person and reached Yuzhen, he heard that Qian's army had withdrawn and expected Tang troops would pursue. He sent Li Chongjin in haste to Zhengyang, saying: "Tang troops are about to arrive; you should strike them quickly."
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang records that during Shizong's personal campaign, at Yuzhen he heard Qian's army had pulled back and expected Zhou forces to pursue. He sent Li Chongjin urgently to Zhengyang with the order: "The enemy is coming—attack at once."

sentences.zh: 彥貞等聞蒨退軍，皆以為怯，裨將鹹師朗曰：「追之可大獲。」

translations.literal: When Liu Yanzhen and the others heard that Qian's army had withdrawn, they all thought it showed cowardice. Deputy General Xian Shilang said: "If we pursue them we can gain a great prize."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzhen and his officers took Qian's withdrawal as a sign of cowardice. Deputy General Xian Shilang urged: "A pursuit would bring rich spoils."

sentences.zh: 劉仁贍使人喻之曰：「君來赴援，未交戰而敵人退，不可測也，慎勿追逐。

translations.literal: Liu Renshan sent someone to instruct him: "You came to give aid. The enemy withdrew before any battle was joined—this is unpredictable. Be careful not to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renshan sent a messenger warning him: "You came as reinforcements. The enemy retreated without fighting—that is suspicious. Do not pursue.

sentences.zh: 君為大將，安危以之，脫有不利，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: As the supreme commander, the army's safety or peril rests on you. If anything goes wrong, the great enterprise will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: You are the commander-in-chief; the fate of the campaign rests on you. One setback could ruin everything."

sentences.zh: 前軍張全約亦曰：「不可追。」

translations.literal: The vanguard commander Zhang Quanyue also said: "Do not pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard commander Zhang Quanyue likewise advised against pursuit."

sentences.zh: 彥貞曰：「軍容在我，汝輩何知？

translations.literal: Liu Yanzhen said: "Military bearing is mine to decide—what do you people know?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzhen snapped: "I command this army—what do you know?

sentences.zh: 沮吾事者斬！」

translations.literal: Whoever discourages my plan shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who stands in my way will be executed!"

sentences.zh: 比至正陽，而重進先至，未及食而戰。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin had already arrived; before they could eat, battle was joined.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin was already there; the armies clashed before the southerners could even take a meal.

sentences.zh: 彥貞施利刃於拒馬，又刻木為獸，號捷馬牌，以皮囊布鐵蒺藜於地。

translations.literal: Liu Yanzhen fitted chevaux-de-frise with sharp blades, carved wooden beasts called "Swift Horse Boards," and spread caltrops on the ground in leather bags.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen armed his abatis with blades, set up carved wooden beasts called Swift Horse Boards, and strewed the ground with bagged caltrops.

sentences.zh: 周兵見而知其怯，一鼓而敗之，彥貞死於陣。）〉

translations.literal: The Zhou troops saw these devices and knew their enemy was timid; at one drum they routed them, and Yanzhen died on the field.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou soldiers saw these tricks and knew their foe lacked nerve; one charge broke them, and Yanzhen fell in battle.)〉

sentences.zh: 殺獲之外，降者三千餘人，皆為我將趙晁所殺。

translations.literal: Apart from those killed and captured, more than three thousand who surrendered were all put to death by our general Zhao Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the dead and captured, more than three thousand who surrendered were slaughtered by the Zhou general Zhao Chao.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，車駕至正陽。

translations.literal: On day jiayin, the imperial carriage reached Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the Emperor arrived at Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 以侍衛都指揮使李重進為淮南道行營都招討使，命宰臣李穀判壽州行府事。

translations.literal: The Commander of the Palace Guards Li Chongjin was made overall commander of the Huainan campaign headquarters, and the chief minister Li Gu was ordered to administer affairs at the Shouzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin, Commander of the Palace Guards, was appointed overall commander of the Huainan campaign, and Chief Minister Li Gu was assigned to run the field headquarters at Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，車駕渡淮。

translations.literal: On day yimao, the imperial carriage crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the Emperor crossed the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，至壽州城下，營於州西北淝水之陽，詔移正陽浮橋於下蔡。

translations.literal: On day bingchen, he reached below Shouzhou city and encamped on the south bank of the Fei River northwest of the prefecture. An edict ordered the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang moved to Xiacai.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he camped south of the Fei River below Shouzhou and ordered the Zhengyang pontoon bridge relocated to Xiacai.

sentences.zh: 庚申，耀兵於城下。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, troops were displayed in force below the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the army paraded in strength before the city walls.

sentences.zh: 〈（《春明退朝錄》云：家有《範魯公雜錄》，記世宗親征忠正，駐蹕城下，中夜有白虹自淝水起，亙數丈，下貫城中，數刻方沒。）〉

translations.literal: (The Record of Leaving Court at Chunming states: Our family has Fan the Duke of Lu's Miscellaneous Records, which records that when Shizong campaigned in person against Zhongzheng and halted below the city, at midnight a white rainbow rose from the Fei River, stretched several zhang, and pierced down into the city; only after several quarters did it vanish.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Record of Leaving Court at Chunming notes that Fan the Duke of Lu's Miscellaneous Records describes Shizong's siege of Shouzhou: at midnight a white rainbow rose from the Fei, spanned several zhang, and plunged into the city before fading after some time.)〉

sentences.zh: 壬戌，今上奏，破淮賊萬餘眾於渦口，斬偽兵馬都監何延錫等，獲戰船五十艘。

translations.literal: On day renxu, Zhao Kuangyin memorialized that he had defeated more than ten thousand Huainan rebels at Wokou, beheaded the false Director of Horse and Foot He Yanxi and others, and captured fifty warships.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Zhao Kuangyin reported victory at Wokou over ten thousand Huainan troops, the execution of the enemy Director of Horse and Foot He Yanxi, and the capture of fifty warships.

sentences.zh: 二月丙寅，幸下蔡。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day bingyin, the Emperor visited Xiacai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingyin, the Emperor went to Xiacai.

sentences.zh: 斬前濟州馬軍都指揮使康儼於路左，坐橋道不謹也。

translations.literal: The former Commander of the Jizhou Horse Army Kang Yi was beheaded on the roadside for negligence regarding bridges and roads.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yi, former commander of the Jizhou horse army, was beheaded beside the road for failing to maintain bridges and routes.

sentences.zh: 朗州節度使王進逵奏，領兵入淮南界。

translations.literal: The military governor of Langzhou Wang Jinkui memorialized that he had led troops into Huainan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinkui, military governor of Langzhou, reported leading his army into Huainan.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，廬壽巡檢使司超奏，破淮賊三千於盛唐，獲都監偽吉州刺史高弼以獻。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, the Luzhou-Shouzhou patrol commissioner Si Chao memorialized that he had defeated three thousand Huainan rebels at Sheng Tang, captured the false Director and false prefect of Jizhou Gao Bi, and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen patrol commissioner Si Chao reported defeating three thousand rebels at Sheng Tang and presenting the captured enemy director and false Jizhou prefect Gao Bi.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him released.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張昭奏，準詔撰集兵法，分為十卷，凡四十二門，目之為《制旨兵法》，上之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Zhao memorialized that, in accordance with an edict, he had compiled military methods in ten juan with forty-two sections in all, entitled Imperially Directed Military Methods, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Zhao presented the ten-juan Imperially Directed Military Methods, comprising forty-two sections compiled at imperial order.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒美，仍以器幣賜之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised him, and he was also given vessels and silks as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued a commendatory edict and rewarded him with ritual vessels and silks.

sentences.zh: 壬申，今上奏，破淮賊萬五千人於清流山，乘勝攻下滁州，擒偽命江州節度使、充行營應援使皇甫暉，常州團練使、充應援都監姚鳳以獻。

translations.literal: On day renshen, Zhao Kuangyin memorialized that he had defeated fifteen thousand Huainan rebels at Qingliushan, pressed the victory to take Chuzhou, and captured the false-appointed military governor of Jiangzhou and campaign relief commander Huangfu Hui and the Changzhou militia commissioner and relief director Yao Feng, whom he presented.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Zhao Kuangyin reported routing fifteen thousand rebels at Qingliushan, capturing Chuzhou, and presenting the captured false Jiangzhou governor and relief commander Huangfu Hui and false Changzhou commissioner and relief director Yao Feng.

sentences.zh: 〈（王銍《默記》：李景聞世宗親至淮上，而滁州其控扼，且援壽州，命大將皇甫暉、監軍姚鳳提兵十萬扼其地。

translations.literal: (From Wang Zhi's Silent Records: When Li Jing heard that Shizong had come in person to the Huai, and that Chuzhou was the strategic choke point and also aided Shouzhou, he ordered the great generals Huangfu Hui and supervising general Yao Feng to lead one hundred thousand troops to hold that place.
translations.idiomatic: (Wang Zhi's Silent Records relates that when Li Jing learned Shizong had reached the Huai in person, he sent Generals Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng with one hundred thousand men to hold Chuzhou, the key to relieving Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖以周師數千與暉遇於清流關隘路，周師大敗，暉整全師入憩滁州城下，會翊日再出。

translations.literal: Taizu led several thousand Zhou troops and met Hui at the Qingliu Pass defile; the Zhou army suffered a great defeat. Hui reassembled his full force and encamped below Chuzhou city, planning to march out again the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin led a few thousand Zhou troops against Hui at Qingliu Pass and was badly beaten. Hui rested his intact army below Chuzhou and planned to march out again the next day.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵聚關下，且虞暉兵再至，聞諸村人，雲有鎮州趙學究在村中教學，多智計，村民有爭訟者，多請以決曲直。

translations.literal: Taizu's troops gathered below the pass, fearing Hui's army would return. He asked the villagers, who said there was a Zhenzhou scholar Zhao in the village who taught school, was full of stratagems, and when villagers had disputes they often asked him to decide right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin's troops regrouped below the pass, anxious that Hui would attack again. Villagers told him of a Zhenzhou schoolmaster Zhao in the hamlet—a man of keen counsel whom locals trusted to settle disputes.

sentences.zh: 太祖往訪之，學究曰：「我有奇計，所謂因敗為勝，轉禍為福。

translations.literal: Taizu went to consult him. The scholar said: "I have a remarkable plan—what is called turning defeat into victory and misfortune into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin sought him out. The schoolmaster said: "I have a plan to turn defeat into victory and disaster into advantage.

sentences.zh: 今關下有徑路，人無行者，雖牌軍亦不知之，乃山之背也，可以直抵城下。

translations.literal: Below the pass there is now a footpath that no one travels—even the guard cavalry do not know it. It is on the reverse slope of the mountain and can reach the city directly.
translations.idiomatic: There is an unused path below the pass, unknown even to the enemy cavalry, along the mountain's far side straight to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 方值西澗水大漲之時，彼必謂我既敗之後，無敢躡其後者，誠能由山背小路率兵浮西澗水至城下，斬關而入，可以得志。」

translations.literal: Just when the West Stream is in flood, they will surely think that after our defeat no one would dare follow them. If you can truly lead troops by the mountain path, ford the West Stream, reach the city, break the gate, and enter, you can achieve your aim."
translations.idiomatic: With the West Stream in flood they will assume we dare not pursue after our rout. Lead men along the back path, ford the stream, and storm the gate—you can still win."

sentences.zh: 太祖大喜，且命學究以指其路，學究亦不辭，而遣人前導，即下令誓師，夜從小徑行，三軍跨馬浮西澗以迫城，暉果不為備。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased and ordered the scholar to point out the route. The scholar did not decline but sent men ahead as guides, then ordered the army sworn for battle. By night they took the small path; the whole army crossed the West Stream on horseback to press the city. Hui indeed was unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin was delighted, had the schoolmaster guide them, and marched by night along the hidden path. The whole army forded the swollen West Stream and rushed the walls while Hui was still unprepared.

sentences.zh: 奪門以入，暉始聞之，率親兵擐甲與太祖巷戰，三縱而三擒之，遂下滁州。）〉

translations.literal: They seized the gate and entered. Only then did Hui hear of it; he led his personal guard in armor to fight Taizu in the streets. Three times he was released and three times captured, and Chuzhou was taken.)〉
translations.idiomatic: They burst through the gate. Hui rallied his guards for street fighting with Kuangyin; three times he was captured and released before Chuzhou fell.)〉

sentences.zh: 甲戌，江南國主李景遣泗州牙將王知朗賫書一函至滁州，本州以聞，書稱唐皇帝奉書於大周皇帝，其略云：「願陳兄事，永奉鄰歡，設或俯鑒遠圖，下交小國，悉班卒乘，俾乂蒼黔，慶雞犬之相聞，奉瓊瑤以為好，必當歲陳山澤之利，少助軍旅之須。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, Li Jing, ruler of Jiangnan, sent the Sizhou adjutant Wang Zhilang bearing one letter to Chuzhou; the prefecture reported it. The letter said the Tang Emperor presents a letter to the Great Zhou Emperor, in summary: "We wish to declare brotherly relations and forever maintain neighborly amity. If you would deign to regard our distant design and condescend to deal with our small state, we would deploy all our soldiers and chariots to bring peace to the black-haired people, rejoice that cock and dog call to one another across the border, and offer jade and treasures in friendship; we would surely present each year the products of mountain and marsh to aid somewhat the needs of your army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Li Jing of Jiangnan sent Adjutant Wang Zhilang to Chuzhou with a letter addressed from the Tang Emperor to the Emperor of Great Zhou, proposing brotherly relations and lasting peace, offering troops to pacify the realm, neighborly contact across the border, jade gifts in friendship, and annual tribute of regional goods to support the Zhou armies.

sentences.zh: 虔俟報章，以答高命，道塗朝坦，禮幣夕行」云。

translations.literal: We reverently await your reply to answer your lofty command; may the roads be clear by morning and gifts sent by evening," it said.
translations.idiomatic: We await your gracious reply; may the roads be open by dawn and our tribute dispatched by nightfall," it concluded.

sentences.zh: 書奏不答。

translations.literal: The memorial of the letter received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The court made no reply to the letter.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，今上縶送所獲江南二將皇甫暉、姚鳳至行在，詔釋之。

translations.literal: On day yihai, Zhao Kuangyin sent under escort the two Jiangnan generals he had captured, Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng, to the imperial camp; an edict ordered their release.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Zhao Kuangyin escorted the captured generals Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng to headquarters, where an edict ordered them freed.

sentences.zh: 壬午，江南國主李景遣其臣偽翰林學士戶部侍郎鐘謨、偽工部侍郎文理院學士李德明等奉表來上，敘願依大國稱臣納貢之意，仍進金器千兩，錦綺綾羅二千匹及禦衣、犀帶、茶茗、藥物等，又進犒軍牛五百頭，酒二千石。

translations.literal: On day renwu, Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his ministers, the false Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Zhong Mo, the false Vice Minister of Works and academician of the Literary and Rational Academy Li Deming, and others to present a memorial stating their wish to submit to the great state as vassals and pay tribute. They also presented one thousand liang of gold vessels, two thousand bolts of brocade and silk, imperial robes, rhinoceros-horn belts, tea, medicines, and the like, and furthermore presented five hundred oxen and two thousand shi of wine to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Li Jing sent Zhong Mo, Li Deming, and other envoys with a memorial offering vassalage and tribute to Great Zhou: a thousand liang of gold vessels, two thousand bolts of silks, imperial robes, rhinoceros belts, tea, medicines, five hundred oxen, and two thousand shi of wine for the troops.

sentences.zh: 是日，賜謨等錦綺綾羅二百匹，銀器一百兩，襲衣、金帶、鞍馬等。

translations.literal: That day, Zhong Mo and the others were given two hundred bolts of brocade and silk, one hundred liang of silver vessels, ceremonial robes, gold belts, saddled horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: That day the envoys received two hundred bolts of silk, a hundred liang of silverware, ceremonial dress, gold belts, and horses.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，侍衛馬軍指揮韓令坤奏，收下揚州。

translations.literal: On day bingxu, the Commander of the Palace Horse Army Han Lingkun memorialized that he had taken Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Han Lingkun, commander of the palace horse army, reported the capture of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略·韓令坤傳》：率兵襲揚州，將吏開門以迎之，令坤整眾而入，市不易肆，人甚悅。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Han Lingkun in Outline History of the Eastern Capital: He led troops in a surprise attack on Yangzhou; the officers opened the gates to welcome him. Lingkun entered with his forces in good order; markets did not change their stalls, and the people were very pleased.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Outline History of the Eastern Capital records that Han Lingkun stormed Yangzhou, whose officers opened the gates to him. He entered in good order without disturbing the markets, to the people's delight.)〉

sentences.zh: 丁亥，壽州城內左神衛軍使徐象等一十八人來奔。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, Xu Xiang, commissioner of the Left Divine Guard Army inside Shouzhou city, and eighteen others came over to the Zhou side.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Xu Xiang of the Left Divine Guard and seventeen others defected from Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，朗州節度使王進逵上言領兵入鄂州界，攻長山寨，殺賊軍三千餘眾。

translations.literal: On day gengyin, the military governor of Langzhou Wang Jinkui reported that he had led troops into Ezhou territory, attacked Changshan Stockade, and killed more than three thousand rebel troops.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Wang Jinkui reported entering Ezhou, storming Changshan Stockade, and killing over three thousand enemy troops.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，今上表偽命天長軍制置使耿謙以本軍降，獲糧草二千餘萬。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, Zhao Kuangyin memorialized that the false-appointed Tianchang Army commissioner Geng Qian had surrendered with his entire force, and more than twenty million units of grain and fodder were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Zhao Kuangyin reported that the false Tianchang commissioner Geng Qian had surrendered with his army, yielding over twenty million units of grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤上言，泰州降。

translations.literal: The Commander of the Palace Horse Army Han Lingkun reported that Taizhou had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun, commander of the palace horse army, reported the surrender of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，荊南上言，朗州節度使王進逵為部將潘叔嗣所殺。

translations.literal: On day guisi, Jingnan reported that the military governor of Langzhou Wang Jinkui had been killed by his subordinate general Pan Shusi.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Jingnan reported that Wang Jinkui of Langzhou had been killed by his subordinate Pan Shusi.

sentences.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王逵傳》：領眾逼宜春，道出長沙，耀兵金波亭，有蜜蜂集傘蓋中，占者以為不利，遂留長沙，令行營副使毛立領兵南下，以潘叔嗣、張文表為前鋒。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Wang Kui in Records of the Nine States: Leading his host to press Yichun, he passed through Changsha and displayed troops at Jinbo Pavilion. Bees gathered on his parasol; diviners deemed this ill-omened. He therefore remained at Changsha and ordered his campaign deputy Mao Li to lead troops south, with Pan Shusi and Zhang Wenbiao as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: (Records of the Nine States records that Wang Kui, marching on Yichun via Changsha, paraded at Jinbo Pavilion. Bees swarmed his parasol—a bad omen—so he stayed in Changsha and sent deputy Mao Li south with Pan Shusi and Zhang Wenbiao in the van.

sentences.zh: 叔嗣怒，至澧陵擁眾而還。

translations.literal: Pan Shusi was angry and, reaching Liling, gathered troops and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Pan Shusi turned back at Liling with his troops.

sentences.zh: 逵聞兵叛，乃乘輕舸奔歸武陵，叔嗣追殺之於朗州城外。）〉

translations.literal: When Kui heard the troops had mutinied, he took a light boat and fled back to Wuling; Shusi pursued and killed him outside Langzhou city.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the mutiny, Kui fled by light boat to Wuling; Shusi overtook and killed him outside Langzhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 遣人詣潭州，請周行逢為帥，行逢至朗州，斬叔嗣於市。

translations.literal: Messengers were sent to Tanzhou to invite Zhou Xingfeng as commander. When Xingfeng reached Langzhou, he beheaded Shusi in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys invited Zhou Xingfeng from Tanzhou to take command; on reaching Langzhou he executed Pan Shusi in public.

sentences.zh: 三月丙申，行光州刺史何超奏，光州偽命都監張承翰以城歸順，尋授承翰集州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day bingshen, the acting prefect of Guangzhou Chao Chao memorialized that the false-appointed director Zhang Chenghan of Guangzhou had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon appointed prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingshen, acting Guangzhou prefect Chao Chao reported that the enemy director Zhang Chenghan had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon made prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，文武百僚再上表請聽樂，詔允之。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, the civil and military officials again submitted a memorial requesting permission to hear music; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the court officials again petitioned for music at court; the Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 行舒州刺史郭令圖奏，收下舒州。

translations.literal: The acting prefect of Shuzhou Guo Lingtu memorialized that he had taken Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Shuzhou prefect Guo Lingtu reported the capture of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 〈（《隆平集·王審琦傳》：世宗征淮，舒州堅壁不下，以郭令圖為刺史，命審琦、司超將兵攻城，一夕拔之。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Wang Shenqi in the Longping Collection: During Shizong's Huainan campaign, Shuzhou held firm and would not yield. Guo Lingtu was made prefect, and Shenqi and Si Chao were ordered to lead troops to attack the city; it was taken in one night.
translations.idiomatic: (The Longping Collection records that during the Huainan campaign Shuzhou resisted stubbornly until Guo Lingtu was appointed prefect and Wang Shenqi and Si Chao stormed it in a single night.

sentences.zh: 令圖入，復見逐於郡人。

translations.literal: When Lingtu entered, he was again driven out by the people of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingtu entered the city, the local populace drove him out again.

sentences.zh: 審琦方進軍援黃州，聞令圖被逐，乃選騎銜枚襲城，夜敗其眾而復納之。）〉

translations.literal: Shenqi was advancing to aid Huangzhou; hearing that Lingtu had been expelled, he selected cavalry who held sticks in their mouths for a night assault on the city, defeated the crowd by night, and reinstalled him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi was marching to relieve Huangzhou; learning of Lingtu's expulsion, he sent cavalry on a silent night raid, routed the rioters, and restored Lingtu to office.)〉

sentences.zh: 江南國主李景表送先隔過朝廷兵士一百五十人至行在。

translations.literal: Li Jing, ruler of Jiangnan, memorialized and sent one hundred fifty soldiers who had previously been cut off from the court army to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Jiangnan returned one hundred fifty Zhou soldiers who had been stranded behind enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 其軍即蜀軍也，秦、鳳之役，為王師所擒，配隸諸軍，及渡淮，輒復南逸。

translations.literal: That army was the Shu army; in the Qin-Feng campaign they had been captured by the imperial army, assigned to various units, and when they crossed the Huai they again fled south.
translations.idiomatic: They were Shu troops captured in the Qin-Feng campaign, assigned to Zhou units, who had fled south again when the army crossed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其奔竄，盡戮之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry at their flight and had them all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged at their desertion, the Emperor had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 丙午，江南國主李景遣其臣偽司空孫晟、偽禮部尚書王崇質等奉表來上，仍進金一千兩、銀十萬兩、羅綺二千匹，又進賞給將士茶絹金銀羅帛等。

translations.literal: On day bingwu, Li Jing sent his ministers, the false Minister of Works Sun Sheng and the false Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi, and others to present a memorial, also presenting one thousand liang of gold, one hundred thousand liang of silver, and two thousand bolts of silk, and furthermore presenting tea, silk, gold, silver, and brocade to reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Li Jing sent Sun Sheng, Wang Chongzhi, and other envoys with a memorial and tribute of a thousand liang of gold, a hundred thousand liang of silver, two thousand bolts of silk, and gifts of tea, silk, and precious goods for the troops.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，兩浙奏，遣大將率兵攻常州。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, the Two Zhes reported that they had sent a great general to lead troops in an attack on Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Two Zhes reported dispatching a senior general to attack Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 延州留後李彥頵奏，蕃眾與部民為亂，尋與兵司都監閻綰掩殺，獲其酋帥高鬧兒等十人，磔於市。

translations.literal: The Yanzhou military commissioner Li Yanyin memorialized that the tribal peoples and local troops had rebelled; soon, together with the Director of the Military Bureau Yan Wan, he launched a surprise attack and killed them, capturing their chieftains Gao Naor and nine others, who were dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou commissioner Li Yanyin reported a tribal uprising; with Director Yan Wan he crushed the rebels, captured ten chieftains including Gao Naor, and had them dismembered in public.

sentences.zh: 彥頵本賈人也，貪而好利，蕃漢之民怨其侵刻，故至於是。

translations.literal: Yanyin was originally a merchant, greedy and fond of profit; both tribal and Han peoples resented his exactions, and thus matters came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyin had been a merchant, greedy and grasping; tribal and Han subjects alike resented his extortions, which led to the revolt.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，賜江南李景書曰：

translations.literal: On day xinhai, an imperial letter was sent to Li Jing of Jiangnan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Emperor sent Li Jing of Jiangnan a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 頃自有唐失禦，天步方艱，巢、蔡喪亂之餘，朱、李戰爭之後，中夏多故，六紀於茲，海縣瓜分，英豪鼎峙，自為聲教，各擅烝黎，連衡而交結四夷，乘釁而憑陵上國。

translations.literal: Recently, since Tang lost the Mandate and the heavenly step grew perilous, after the disorders of Huang Chao and Cai Jing, and after the wars of Zhu and Li, the Central Plain has known many troubles for six decades now. The realm has been carved like a melon; heroes stand like tripods, each proclaiming his own culture and each monopolizing the people. They allied horizontally and made friends with the four barbarians, seizing opportunities to encroach on the central state.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang lost the Mandate the realm has known sixty years of turmoil—from the catastrophes of Huang Chao and Cai Jing through the wars of Zhu Wen and Li Keyong. The empire was carved among rival warlords, each ruling his own domain, allying with barbarian powers and pressing the central state whenever weakness appeared.

sentences.zh: 華風不競，否運所鐘，凡百有心，孰不興憤？

translations.literal: Chinese civilization could not contend; the age of obstruction had struck. Among all who had hearts, who did not rise in indignation?
translations.idiomatic: Chinese civilization seemed spent and fortune had turned against us—who with a heart did not burn with anger?

sentences.zh: 朕猥承先訓，恭荷永圖，德不迨於前王，道不方於往古。

translations.literal: We humbly received our ancestors' instruction and reverently bear the eternal design, yet our virtue does not reach the former kings nor our Way equal that of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I have humbly inherited my forebears' charge and their long design, though my virtue falls short of the sage kings and my governance cannot match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 然而擅一百州之富庶，握三十萬之甲兵，且農戰交修，士卒樂用，思欲報累朝之宿怨，刷萬姓之包羞。

translations.literal: Yet we monopolize the wealth of a hundred prefectures and hold three hundred thousand armored troops; both farming and warfare are cultivated together, and soldiers are glad to serve. We think to repay the accumulated wrongs of many reigns and wash away the shame wrapped around the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I command the wealth of a hundred prefectures and three hundred thousand armed men; agriculture and war are pursued together, and the troops are eager to fight. I mean to avenge generations of humiliation and restore the people's honor.

sentences.zh: 是以踐位已來，懷安不暇，破幽、并之巨寇，收秦、鳳之全封，兵不告疲，民有餘力。

translations.literal: Therefore since taking the throne we have had no leisure for ease: we broke the great bandits of You and Bing and recovered the full territory of Qin and Feng; the army has not complained of fatigue and the people still have surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession I have known no ease: I crushed the great enemies of You and Bing and recovered Qin and Feng intact; the army has not wearied and the people still have strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 一昨回軍隴上，問罪江幹，我實有辭，咎將誰執？

translations.literal: Just recently we turned the army from Longyou and called you to account on the river bank. We truly have grounds; upon whom will blame fall?
translations.idiomatic: Having just returned from Longyou, I now bring the army to the Yangtze to call you to account. The grievance is mine—who else bears the blame?

sentences.zh: 朕親提金鼓，尋渡淮、淝，上順天心，下符人欲，前鋒所向，彼眾無遺，棄甲僵屍，動盈川谷。

translations.literal: We personally took up drums and gongs and soon crossed the Huai and Fei. Above we accord with Heaven's heart; below we match the people's desire. Wherever the vanguard turned, none of their host remained; cast-off armor and stiff corpses filled valleys and streams.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken the field in person, crossed the Huai and Fei, and aligned Heaven's will with the people's desire. Where my vanguard advanced, the enemy left none alive—abandoned armor and corpses choked the valleys.

sentences.zh: 收城徇地，已過滁陽，豈有落其爪牙，折其羽翼，潰其心腹，扼其吭喉而不亡者哉！

translations.literal: We have taken cities and overrun lands, already passing Chuyang. How could there be one whose claws and fangs are removed, whose wings are broken, whose heart and belly are routed, whose throat is gripped, and yet does not perish!
translations.idiomatic: Cities have fallen and territory been overrun as far as Chuyang. With your claws cut, wings broken, heart routed, and throat in my grip—how can you not perish?

sentences.zh: 蚤者，泗州主將遞送到書一函；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Sizhou commander forwarded one letter;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier your Sizhou commander forwarded a letter;

sentences.zh: 尋又使人鐘謨、李德明至，賫所上表及貢奉衣服腰帶、金銀器幣、茶藥牛酒等；

translations.literal: soon after, envoys Zhong Mo and Li Deming arrived, bearing the memorial you submitted and tribute of robes, belts, gold and silver vessels, tea, medicines, oxen, wine, and the like;
translations.idiomatic: then Zhong Mo and Li Deming came with your memorial and gifts of robes, belts, gold and silver, tea, medicines, oxen, and wine;

sentences.zh: 今又使人孫晟等並到行朝。

translations.literal: now envoys Sun Sheng and others have all reached the imperial camp as well.
translations.idiomatic: and now Sun Sheng and your other envoys have reached headquarters.

sentences.zh: 觀其降身聽命，引咎告窮，所謂君子見機，不俟終日，茍非達識，孰能若斯？

translations.literal: Observing how you lower yourself to heed commands, admit fault, and declare your extremity—this is what is called the gentleman perceiving the moment and not waiting for the full day. If one is not far-sighted, who could act thus?
translations.idiomatic: You humble yourself, accept blame, and confess your plight—the wise man seizes the moment without delay. Only a man of insight would act as you have.

sentences.zh: 但以奮武興戎，所以討不服；

translations.literal: Yet to rouse martial valor and raise arms is how one punishes those who will not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Yet arms are raised to chastise the recalcitrant;

sentences.zh: 惇信明義，所以懷遠人。

translations.literal: to be sincere in faith and clear in righteousness is how one win over those far away.
translations.idiomatic: while sincerity and righteousness are how distant peoples are won over.

sentences.zh: 五帝三王盛德大業，恒用此道，以正萬邦。

translations.literal: The great virtue and great enterprise of the Five Emperors and Three Kings always used this Way to set the myriad states right.
translations.idiomatic: The sage rulers of antiquity always governed the realm by this same principle.

sentences.zh: 朕今躬統戎師，龔行討伐，告於郊廟社稷，詢於將相公卿，天誘其衷，國無異論。

translations.literal: We now personally command the army and reverently carry out punitive expedition, announcing it to the suburban altars, ancestral temples, and altars of soil and grain, consulting generals, ministers, and chief officials. Heaven guides our heart, and the state has no dissenting views.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead the army in person on this punitive campaign, having announced it to the spirits and consulted my ministers. Heaven guides my purpose, and the court speaks with one voice.

sentences.zh: 茍不能恢復內地，申畫邊疆，便議班旋，真同戲劇，則何以光祖宗之烈，厭士庶之心，匪獨違天，兼且咈眾。

translations.literal: If we cannot recover the inner lands and extend the frontier demarcation, yet discuss withdrawing the army, it would truly be like a play—how then could we glorify our ancestors' achievements or satisfy the hearts of officers and commoners? This would not only defy Heaven but also go against the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: To withdraw before recovering our territory and securing the border would be mere theater—how could I honor our ancestors or satisfy army and people? That would defy Heaven and outrage the nation.

sentences.zh: 但以淮南部內，已定六州，盧、壽、濠、黃，大軍悉集，指期克日，拉朽焚枯，其餘數城，非足介意。

translations.literal: Yet within southern Huainan, six prefectures are already settled—Lu, Shou, Hao, Huang—and the great army is fully assembled. A set day for victory is fixed; rotten wood will be pulled down and dry stalks burned. The remaining few cities are not worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: Six prefectures south of the Huai are already secured; Lu, Shou, Hao, and Huang are invested by our main force, victory is imminent, and the few cities still holding out scarcely matter.

sentences.zh: 必若盡淮甸之土地，為大國之提封，猶是遠圖，豈同迷復。

translations.literal: If you must have all the land of the Huai region as the great state's frontier, that is still a far-reaching design—how could it be the same as losing your way and returning?
translations.idiomatic: To annex all Huainan into our empire is a far-sighted aim—not the folly of turning back in confusion.

sentences.zh: 如此則江南吏卒悉遣放還，江北軍民並當留住，免違物類之性，俾安鄉土之情。

translations.literal: Thus all officials and soldiers of Jiangnan would be sent back, while military and civilians north of the river would all remain, avoiding violation of creatures' nature and allowing attachment to native soil.
translations.idiomatic: Southern officials and troops would be sent home; northerners would remain where they belong, respecting natural ties to native soil.

sentences.zh: 至於削去尊稱，願輸臣禮，非無故事，實有前規。

translations.literal: As for removing exalted titles and wishing to render ministerial rites, this is not without precedent; there truly are former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendering your royal title and accepting vassal status is not without precedent.

sentences.zh: 蕭詧奉周，不失附庸之道；

translations.literal: Xiao Cha served Zhou without failing the way of a dependent state;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha served the Zhou as a loyal vassal;

sentences.zh: 孫權事魏，自同藩國之儀。

translations.literal: Sun Quan served Wei and himself adopted the ceremonies of a feudatory state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan served Wei with the rites proper to a feudatory prince.

sentences.zh: 古也雖然，今則不取，但存常號，何爽歲寒。

translations.literal: Ancient times were thus, but today we do not accept it; we will only preserve your ordinary title—how could this conflict with the steadfast pine in winter cold?
translations.idiomatic: Such was antiquity, but I will not demand it now; your ordinary title may stand—no breach of constancy through winter's cold.

sentences.zh: 儻堅事大之心，終不迫人於險，事資真愨，辭匪枝遊，俟諸郡之悉來，即大軍之立罷。

translations.literal: If you firmly maintain a heart of serving the great power, we will never drive you to extremity. Matters depend on true sincerity; words must not be branching evasions. When all prefectures have submitted, the great army will immediately be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: If you remain steadfast in submission, I will not press you to the brink. Deal in sincerity, not evasive words. When every prefecture has surrendered, the army will withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 質於天地，信若丹青，我無彼欺，爾無我詐，言盡於此，更不煩雲，茍曰未然，請自茲絕。

translations.literal: We pledge before Heaven and Earth, faith like vermilion on silk: I will not deceive you, you will not cheat me. Words end here; no further verbosity. If you say it is not so, let us break off from this moment.
translations.idiomatic: I swear before Heaven and Earth, as clear as ink on silk: no deceit between us. I have said enough. If you disagree, let all relations end here.

sentences.zh: 竊以陽春在候，庶務縈思，願無廢於節宣，更自期於愛重。

translations.literal: We venture to note that spring is at hand and many affairs fill the mind. We hope you will not neglect moderation in conduct and will further cherish your own well-being.
translations.idiomatic: Spring is near and affairs press upon you; take care of your health and cherish yourself.

sentences.zh: 音塵非遠，風壤猶殊，翹想所深，勞於夢寐。

translations.literal: Our messages are not far apart, yet customs and soil still differ. Our earnest longing runs deep and wearies us even in dreams.
translations.idiomatic: Though not far apart in distance, our lands differ in custom; my thoughts of you weary me even in sleep.

sentences.zh: 又賜其將佐書曰：

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to their generals and aides, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also sent their commanders a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 朕自類祃出師，麾旄問罪，絕長淮而電擊，指建業以鷹揚，旦夕之間，克捷相繼。

translations.literal: Since we took the army out at the border sacrifice, we have raised banners to call to account, struck like lightning across the long Huai, and aimed at Jianye like a soaring hawk. Within days victories have followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the field at the border sacrifice, my banners have marched to punish rebellion, swept the Huai like lightning, and borne down on Jianye like a hawk. Victories have followed in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 至若兵興之所自，釁起之所來，勝負之端倪，戎甲之次第，不勞盡諭，必想具知。

translations.literal: As for when arms were first raised, when the provocation arose, the signs of victory and defeat, and the sequence of campaigns—there is no need to explain fully; you surely know it all.
translations.idiomatic: The origins of this war, its provocations, and the course of battle need no lengthy explanation—you know them well.

sentences.zh: 近者金陵使人，繼來行闕，追悔前事，委質大朝，非無謝咎之辭，亦有罷軍之請，但以南邦之土地，本中夏之封疆，茍失克復之期，大辜朝野之望，已興是役，固不徒還，必若自淮以南，畫江為界，盡歸中國，猶是遠圖。

translations.literal: Recently envoys from Jinling have come in succession to the imperial camp, regretting past deeds and submitting to the great court. There are words of apology and requests to halt the army, but the southern state's lands were originally the Central Plain's territory. If we miss the time for recovery, we greatly betray court and people's hopes. Having raised this campaign, we surely will not return empty-handed. If all south of the Huai, with the Yangtze as boundary, returns to China, that is still a far-reaching design.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Jinling have come repeatedly, repenting and suing for peace—but the south was always Chinese soil. To withdraw now would betray the hopes of court and army. This campaign will not end in vain. To restore all lands south of the Huai to the empire remains our true aim.

sentences.zh: 所雲願為外臣，乞比湖、浙，彼既服義，朕豈忍人，必當別議封崇，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: What is said about wishing to be an outer minister and begging comparison with Hu and Zhe—since they have submitted to righteousness, how could We bear to press men? We will certainly discuss separate enfeoffment and treat them with special ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Your offer to become an outer vassal like the rulers of Hu and Zhe—once you submit in good faith, I will not be harsh. I shall grant you honorable rank and special treatment.

sentences.zh: 凡爾將佐，各盡乃心，善為國家之謀，勉擇恒久之利。

translations.literal: All you generals and aides, each give your full heart, plan well for the state, and strive to choose lasting advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Each of you commanders should give your full counsel, serve your state's true interest, and choose what will endure.

sentences.zh: 初，李景遣鐘謨、李德明奉表至行闕，使人面奏云：「本國主願割壽、濠、泗、楚、光、海六州之地，歸於大朝。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Jing sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial to the imperial camp. Their envoy reported in person: "Our ruler wishes to cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai to the great court."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jing had sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial; their envoy reported that Li Jing offered to cede Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai to Great Zhou."

sentences.zh: 帝志在盡取江北諸郡，不允其請。

translations.literal: The Emperor's aim was to take all prefectures north of the river and did not grant the request.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor aimed to take all territory north of the Yangtze and refused.

sentences.zh: 使人見王師急攻壽陽，李德明奏曰：「願陛下寬臣數日之誅，容臣自往江南，取本國表，盡獻江北之地。」

translations.literal: The envoy saw the imperial army pressing the attack on Shouyang. Li Deming memorialized: "We beg Your Majesty to spare our lives for a few days and allow us to go ourselves to Jiangnan, obtain our state's memorial, and offer all lands north of the river."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the assault on Shouyang, Li Deming pleaded: "Grant us a few days' reprieve to return south, obtain our ruler's formal submission, and surrender all territory north of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 帝許之，乃令李德明、王崇質賫此書以賜李景。

translations.literal: The Emperor consented and ordered Li Deming and Wang Chongzhi to bear this letter and present it to Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and sent Li Deming and Wang Chongzhi to deliver this letter to Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲子，以徐州節度使武行德為濠州城下行營都部署，以前鄧州節度使候章為壽州城下水寨都部署。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, day jiazi, the military governor of Xuzhou Wu Xingde was made overall commander of the encampment below Hao Prefecture city, and the former military governor of Dengzhou Hou Zhang was made commander of the water stockade below Shou Prefecture city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on jiazi, Wu Xingde of Xuzhou was appointed commander below Hao city, and former Dengzhou governor Hou Zhang commander of the water camp below Shou city.

sentences.zh: 己巳，車駕發壽春，循淮而東。

translations.literal: On day jisi, the imperial carriage departed Shouchun and followed the Huai eastward.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the Emperor left Shouchun and marched east along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 辛未，揚州奏，江南大破兩浙軍於常州。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, Yangzhou reported that Jiangnan had routed the Two Zhes' army at Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Yangzhou reported that Jiangnan had crushed the Two Zhes' army at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，兩浙錢俶承詔遣部將率兵攻常州，為江南大將陸孟俊所敗，將佐陷沒者甚眾，李景亦以表聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qian Chu of the Two Zhes, obeying an edict, had sent a subordinate general to lead troops against Changzhou but was defeated by the Jiangnan great general Lu Mengjun; many officers were lost. Li Jing also reported this in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chu of the Two Zhes had attacked Changzhou at imperial order but was beaten by Lu Mengjun; many officers were lost. Li Jing reported the victory to the Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，駐蹕於濠州城下。

translations.literal: On day yihai, the Emperor halted below Hao Prefecture city.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Emperor encamped below Hao city.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，揚州韓令坤破江南賊軍於州之東境，獲大將陸孟俊。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Han Lingkun of Yangzhou defeated the Jiangnan rebel army on the eastern border of the prefecture and captured the great general Lu Mengjun.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Han Lingkun of Yangzhou routed Jiangnan forces on the eastern border and captured Lu Mengjun.

sentences.zh: 今上表大破江南軍於六合，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin memorialized that he had routed the Jiangnan army at Liuhe, taking five thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin reported a great victory at Liuhe with five thousand enemy heads taken.

sentences.zh: 時李景乘常州之捷，遣陸孟俊領兵迫泰州，王師不守，韓令坤欲棄揚州而回。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jing, riding the victory at Changzhou, sent Lu Mengjun to lead troops against Taizhou. The imperial army did not hold firm, and Han Lingkun wished to abandon Yangzhou and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by Changzhou, Li Jing sent Lu Mengjun against Taizhou. Zhou forces wavered, and Han Lingkun considered abandoning Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，急遣殿前都指揮使張永德帥親兵往援之，又命今上領步騎二千人屯於六合。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and urgently sent the Commander of the Palace Front Army Zhang Yongde to lead personal troops to their aid, and also ordered Zhao Kuangyin to lead two thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the Emperor sent Zhang Yongde with the palace guard to reinforce them and ordered Zhao Kuangyin to camp at Liuhe with two thousand horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 俄而陸孟俊領其徒自海陵抵揚州，令坤迎擊，敗之，生擒孟俊。

translations.literal: Soon Lu Mengjun led his followers from Hailing to Yangzhou. Lingkun met and attacked them, defeated them, and captured Mengjun alive.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mengjun marched from Hailing on Yangzhou; Lingkun met him, routed his force, and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 李景遣其弟齊王達率大眾由瓜步濟江，距六合一舍而設柵。

translations.literal: Li Jing sent his younger brother the Prince of Qi, Li Da, to lead a great host across the river at Guabu, encamping one li from Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing sent his brother Li Da, Prince of Qi, with a large army across the river at Guabu, encamping a li from Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 居數日，乃棄柵來迫官軍。

translations.literal: After several days they abandoned the stockade and came to press the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they abandoned their camp and advanced on the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 今上麾兵以擊之，賊軍大敗，餘眾赴江溺死者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin commanded troops to attack them; the rebel army suffered a great defeat, and the remainder who rushed into the river and drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin attacked; the enemy was routed, and countless drowned fleeing into the river.

sentences.zh: 己卯，韓令坤奏，敗楚州賊將馬在貴萬餘眾於灣頭堰，獲漣州刺史秦進崇。

translations.literal: On day jimao, Han Lingkun memorialized that he had defeated more than ten thousand troops of the Chuzhou rebel general Ma Zaigui at Wantou Weir and captured the prefect of Lianzhou Qin Jinchong.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Han Lingkun reported defeating over ten thousand men under the Chuzhou rebel Ma Zaigui at Wantou Weir and capturing Lianzhou prefect Qin Jinchong.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以宣徽南院使向訓為權淮南節度使，充沿江招討使；

translations.literal: On day bingxu, the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting military governor of Huainan and riverine campaign commander;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Xiang Xun of the Southern Bureau was made acting Huainan governor and riverine campaign commander;

sentences.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤充沿江副招討使。

translations.literal: the Commander of the Palace Horse Army Han Lingkun was made deputy riverine campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun, commander of the palace horse army, was made his deputy.

sentences.zh: 〈（《宋史·向拱傳》：揚州初平，南唐令境上出師謀收復，韓令坤有棄城之意，即驛召拱赴行在，拜淮南節度使，依前宣徽使兼沿江招討使，以令坤為副。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Xiang Gong in the History of Song: When Yangzhou was first pacified, Southern Tang ordered troops on the border to march and plan recovery. Han Lingkun intended to abandon the city. Gong was summoned by post horse to the imperial camp, appointed military governor of Huainan, retaining his former post as commissioner while also serving as riverine campaign commander, with Lingkun as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Song records that after Yangzhou fell, Southern Tang mobilized to retake it and Han Lingkun wished to evacuate. Xiang Gong was summoned, made Huainan governor and riverine commander, with Lingkun as deputy.

sentences.zh: 時周師久駐淮陽，都將趙晁、白延遇等驕恣橫暴，不相稟從，惟務貪濫，至有劫人婦女者。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou army had long encamped at Huaiyang; commanders Zhao Chao, Bai Yanyu, and others were arrogant, violent, and insubordinate, devoted only to greed and excess, even seizing other men's wives and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army had long camped at Huaiyang; commanders Zhao Chao and Bai Yanyu were insubordinate and rapacious, even abducting women.

sentences.zh: 及拱至，戮其不法者數輩，軍中肅然。）〉

translations.literal: When Gong arrived, he executed several lawless men and the army became orderly.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Gong executed several offenders and restored discipline.)〉

sentences.zh: 丁亥，車駕發濠州，幸渦口。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, the imperial carriage departed Hao Prefecture and proceeded to Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the Emperor left Hao and went to Wokou.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以前湖南節度使馬希崇為左羽林統軍。

translations.literal: On day jichou, the former military governor of Hunan Ma Xichong was made Commander of the Left Feathered Forest Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou former Hunan governor Ma Xichong was appointed commander of the Left Feathered Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 五月壬辰朔，以渦口為鎮淮軍。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, day renchen, Wokou was made Zhenhuai Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month Wokou was designated Zhenhuai Army.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕還京，發渦口。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, the imperial carriage returned to the capital, departing from Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the Emperor returned to the capital from Wokou.

sentences.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》：天子駐於渦口，猶欲再幸揚州，宰相範質以師老泣諫，乃班師。）〉

translations.literal: (From Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang: The Son of Heaven halted at Wokou and still wished to visit Yangzhou again. The chief minister Fan Zhi remonstrated with tears that the army was weary, and only then did they withdraw.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling records that at Wokou the Emperor still wished to march on Yangzhou until Fan Zhi tearfully pleaded that the army was exhausted, whereupon he withdrew.)〉

sentences.zh: 乙卯，上至自淮南，詔赦都下見禁罪人。

translations.literal: On day yimao, the Emperor arrived from Huainan and issued an edict pardoning prisoners under detention in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the Emperor returned from Huainan and pardoned prisoners held in the capital.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，陳州節度使王令溫卒。

translations.literal: On day dingsi, the military governor of Chenzhou Wang Lingwen died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Wang Lingwen, military governor of Chenzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以江南偽命東都副留守、工部侍郎馮延魯為太府卿。

translations.literal: On day wuwu, the false-appointed Eastern Capital deputy regent and Vice Minister of Works Feng Yanlu of Jiangnan was made Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Feng Yanlu, the former Southern Tang deputy regent of the Eastern Capital, was appointed Director of the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 己未，太子賓客於德辰卒。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, the Crown Prince's Mentor Yu Dechen died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Yu Dechen, mentor to the Crown Prince, died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔：「天下公私織造布帛及諸色匹段，幅尺斤兩，並須依向來制度，不得輕弱假偽，犯者擒捉送官。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, an edict stated: "Throughout the realm, whether in public or private weaving of cloth and all kinds of textile pieces, width, length, and weight must all follow the established regulations. Light, weak, or counterfeit goods are forbidden. Offenders shall be seized and sent to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou an edict required all cloth and textiles, public or private, to meet established standards of width and weight; light or counterfeit goods were forbidden, offenders to be arrested.

sentences.zh: 六月甲子，以鳳翔節度使王景為秦州節度使，兼西面沿邊都部署；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, day jiazi, the military governor of Fengxiang Wang Jing was made military governor of Qinzhou and overall commander of the western frontier;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Wang Jing of Fengxiang was made Qinzhou governor and overall western frontier commander;

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使、陳州節度使向訓為淮南節度使，依前南院宣徽使，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau and military governor of Chenzhou Xiang Xun was made military governor of Huainan, retaining his former post as Southern Bureau commissioner, with the added title of Grand Preceptor by inspection;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun was confirmed as Huainan governor, retaining his commissioner post, with the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor;

sentences.zh: 以曹州節度使韓通為許州節度使，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: the military governor of Caozhou Han Tong was made military governor of Xuzhou, with the added title of Grand Preceptor by inspection;
translations.idiomatic: Han Tong of Caozhou was transferred to Xuzhou with the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor;

sentences.zh: 以亳州防禦使王全斌為隴州防禦使，遙領利州昭武軍兩使留後。

translations.literal: the defense commissioner of Bozhou Wang Quanbin was made defense commissioner of Longzhou and held concurrently the post of acting commissioner of the two offices of Lizhou Zhaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quanbin of Bozhou was made Longzhou defense commissioner and concurrently acting commissioner of Lizhou Zhaowu Army.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，許州王彥超移鎮永興軍，鄧州田景鹹移鎮鄜州。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, Wang Yanchao of Xuzhou was transferred to Yongxing Army, and Tian Jingxian of Dengzhou was transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Wang Yanchao was transferred from Xuzhou to Yongxing, and Tian Jingxian from Dengzhou to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞楊昭儉、知雜侍御史趙礪、侍御史張糾並停任，坐鞫獄失實也。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Yang Zhaojian, the supervising attendant censor Zhao Li, and the attendant censor Zhang Jiu were all suspended for errors in conducting criminal investigations.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yang Zhaojian, supervising censor Zhao Li, and attendant censor Zhang Jiu were suspended for mishandling criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎陶穀為兵部侍郎，充翰林學士承旨；

translations.literal: On day dingmao, the Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Tao Gu was made Vice Minister of War and Chief Hanlin academician;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Tao Gu was made Vice Minister of War and chief Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以水部員外郎知制誥扈載、度支員外郎王著，並本官充翰林學士；

translations.literal: the Vice Director of the Water Bureau and drafter of edicts Hu Zai and the Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau Wang Zhu were both made Hanlin academicians while retaining their original offices;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zai of the Water Bureau and Wang Zhu of the Revenue Bureau were appointed Hanlin academicians while keeping their posts;

sentences.zh: 以給事中高防為右散騎常侍；

translations.literal: the Supervising Secretary Gao Fang was made Right Regular Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Gao Fang was made Right Regular Attendant;

sentences.zh: 以前都官郎中、知制誥薛居正為左諫議大夫，充昭文館學士，判館事。

translations.literal: the former Director of the Bureau of Justice and drafter of edicts Xue Juzheng was made Left Remonstrance Grand Master, Hanlin academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and administrator of the hall's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: former Bureau of Justice director Xue Juzheng was made Left Remonstrance Grand Master, Zhaowen Hall academician, and hall administrator.

sentences.zh: 壬申，曲赦淮南道諸州見禁罪人，自今年六月十一日已前，凡有違犯，無問輕重，並不窮問。

translations.literal: On day renshen, a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners under detention in all prefectures of the Huainan circuit. For offenses before the eleventh day of the sixth month of this year, regardless of severity, no further investigation would be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen a partial amnesty covered all prisoners in Huainan prefectures for offenses before the eleventh of the sixth month, without regard to severity.

sentences.zh: 先屬江南之時，應有非理科徭，無名配率，一切停罷雲。

translations.literal: For the period when they had belonged to Jiangnan, all improper corvée levies and nameless additional assessments were to be entirely halted.
translations.idiomatic: All improper levies imposed under Jiangnan rule were abolished.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以右衛上將軍扈彥珂為太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, the General of the Right Guard Hu Yanke was made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Hu Yanke, general of the Right Guard, was made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and retired.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以西京留守王晏為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: On day gengchen, the Western Capital regent Wang Yan was made military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Western Capital regent Wang Yan was appointed military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 戊子，升贍國軍為濱州。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Shanguo Army was promoted to Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Shanguo Army was elevated to Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淮南道招討使李重進奏，壽州賊軍攻南寨，王師不利。

translations.literal: The Huainan campaign commander Li Chongjin memorialized that the Shouzhou rebel army had attacked the southern stockade and the imperial army had fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin reported that Shouzhou rebels had attacked the southern camp and the imperial army had suffered a setback.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔步軍都指揮使李繼勛營於壽州之南，攻賊壘。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Commander of the Foot Army Li Jixun had been ordered to encamp south of Shouzhou and attack the rebel fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jixun, commander of the foot army, had been ordered to camp south of Shouzhou and assault the rebel works.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊軍出城來攻我軍，破柵而入，其攻城之具並為賊所焚，將士死者數百人。

translations.literal: That day the rebel army came out of the city to attack our army, broke through the palisade and entered, and all siege equipment was burned by the rebels; several hundred officers and soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: That day the rebels sallied, broke into the camp, burned the siege equipment, and killed several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 李重進在東寨，亦不能救。

translations.literal: Li Chongjin was in the eastern stockade and likewise could not rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin in the eastern camp could not relieve them.

sentences.zh: 時城堅未下，師老於外，加之暑毒，糧運不繼。

translations.literal: At that time the city walls were strong and had not fallen; the army was weary from long campaigning abroad, and in addition there was summer heat and poison; grain transport did not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: The city still held; the army was weary, summer heat was severe, and supplies ran short.

sentences.zh: 李繼勛喪失之後，軍無固誌，諸將議欲退軍，賴今上自六合領兵歸闕，過其城下，因為駐留旬日，王師復振。

translations.literal: After Li Jixun's defeat the army had no firm resolve; the generals discussed withdrawing. Thanks to Zhao Kuangyin leading troops back to the capital from Liuhe and passing below the city, he stayed for ten days on that account, and the imperial army revived.
translations.idiomatic: After Jixun's defeat morale collapsed and officers talked of retreat. Zhao Kuangyin, returning from Liuhe, halted below the city for ten days and restored the army's spirit.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛卯朔，以武清軍節度使、知潭州軍府事周行逢為朗州大都督，充武平軍節度使，加檢校太尉、兼侍中。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, first day xinmao, the military governor of Wuqing Army and administrator of Tanzhou military affairs Zhou Xingfeng was made Grand Commander of Langzhou and military governor of Wuping Army, with the added titles of Grand Preceptor by inspection and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month Zhou Xingfeng was made Langzhou commander and Wuping governor, with the honorary ranks of Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以太子賓客盧價為禮部尚書致仕，以給事中李明為大理卿。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, the Crown Prince's Mentor Lu Jia was made Minister of Rites and retired; the Supervising Secretary Li Ming was made Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Lu Jia, mentor to the Crown Prince, retired as Minister of Rites; Supervising Secretary Li Ming was made director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 庚子，盧州行營都部署劉重進奏，破淮賊千餘於州界。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, the overall commander of the Luzhou campaign headquarters Liu Chongjin memorialized that he had defeated more than a thousand Huainan rebels on the prefectural border.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Liu Chongjin reported defeating over a thousand Huainan rebels on the Luzhou border.

sentences.zh: 丁未，濠州行營都部署武行德奏，敗淮賊二千人於州界。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, the overall commander of the Hao Prefecture campaign headquarters Wu Xingde memorialized that he had defeated two thousand Huainan rebels on the prefectural border.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Wu Xingde reported defeating two thousand Huainan rebels on the Hao border.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，太子太保王仁裕卒。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, the Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince Wang Renyu died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Wang Renyu, Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince, died.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，皇后符氏薨。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, the Empress née Fu died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Empress Fu died.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使向訓自揚州班師，回駐壽春。

translations.literal: The military governor of Huainan Xiang Xun withdrew his army from Yangzhou and returned to encamp at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan governor Xiang Xun withdrew from Yangzhou and re-encamped at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 時王師攻壽春，經年未下，江、淮盜賊充斥，舒、蘄、和、泰等州復為吳人所據，故棄揚州並力於壽春焉。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army had attacked Shouchun for a year without taking it; bandits filled the Yangtze and Huai regions, and Shu, Qi, He, Tai, and other prefectures had again been seized by Wu men. Therefore Yangzhou was abandoned to concentrate force on Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Shouchun had dragged on a year; bandits infested the rivers, and Wu forces had retaken Shu, Qi, He, and Tai. Yangzhou was abandoned to concentrate on Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》：向訓請棄揚州，並力以攻壽春，乃封府庫付主者，遣淮南舊將按巡城中，秋毫不犯而去。

translations.literal: (From Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang: Xiang Xun requested abandoning Yangzhou to concentrate force on attacking Shouchun. He sealed the treasury and entrusted it to custodians, sent former Huainan generals to patrol the city, and withdrew without violating so much as an autumn hair.
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling records that Xiang Xun asked to abandon Yangzhou and focus on Shouchun, sealed the treasury, posted former Huainan officers to keep order, and withdrew without harming the populace.

sentences.zh: 淮人大悅，皆負糗糧以送周師。）〉

translations.literal: The Huai people were greatly pleased and all carried dry rations to send off the Zhou army.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced and brought provisions to supply the Zhou army.)〉

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，河陽白重贊移鎮涇州，張澤移鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, day renxu, Bai Chongzan of Heyang was transferred to Jingzhou, and Zhang Ze was transferred to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renxu, Bai Chongzan was transferred from Heyang to Jingzhou and Zhang Ze to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以前鄧州節度使侯章復為鄧州節度使，以侍衛步軍都指揮使、彰信軍節度使李繼勛為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, the former military governor of Dengzhou Hou Zhang was again made military governor of Dengzhou, and the Commander of the Palace Foot Army and military governor of Zhangxin Army Li Jixun was made military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Hou Zhang was restored to Dengzhou, and Li Jixun, commander of the palace foot army, was made Heyang governor.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，太僕卿劇可久停任，坐為舉官累也。

translations.literal: On day yichou, the Director of the Imperial Stud Ju Kejiu was suspended for being implicated through a nominee he had recommended.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Ju Kejiu, Director of the Imperial Stud, was suspended for a nominee's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，端明殿學士王樸撰成新歷上之，命曰《顯德欽天曆》，上親為制序，仍付司天監行用。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, the Duanming Hall academician Wang Pu completed a new calendar and presented it. It was named the Xiande Imperial Heaven Calendar. The Emperor personally composed the preface and ordered the Directorate of Astronomy to put it into use.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wang Pu presented the new Xiande Imperial Heaven Calendar; the Emperor wrote its preface and ordered the Directorate of Astronomy to adopt it.

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使張永德奏，破淮賊於下蔡。

translations.literal: The Commander of the Palace Front Army Zhang Yongde memorialized that he had defeated the Huainan rebels at Xiacai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde, commander of the palace front army, reported defeating Huainan rebels at Xiacai.

sentences.zh: 先是，江南李景以王師猶在壽州，遣其將林仁肇、郭廷謂率水陸軍至下蔡，欲奪浮梁，以舟實薪芻，乘風縱火，永德禦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Jing of Jiangnan, because the imperial army was still at Shouzhou, sent his generals Lin Renzhao and Guo Tingyu to lead land and naval forces to Xiacai, intending to seize the pontoon bridge. They loaded boats with firewood and fodder and, riding the wind, set fires. Yongde defended against them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing had sent Lin Renzhao and Guo Tingyu with a combined force to Xiacai to seize the pontoon bridge, loading fire ships with fuel; Zhang Yongde held them off.

sentences.zh: 有頃，風勢倒指，賊眾稍卻，因為官軍所敗。

translations.literal: Before long the wind shifted direction, the rebel host fell back somewhat, and they were therefore defeated by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the wind turned, the enemy fell back, and the imperial army routed them.

sentences.zh: 己卯，工部侍郎王敏停任，坐薦子婿陳南金為河陽記室也。

translations.literal: On day jimao, the Vice Minister of Works Wang Min was suspended for recommending his son-in-law Chen Nanjin as recorder of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Vice Minister of Works Wang Min was suspended for appointing his son-in-law Chen Nanjin as recorder at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 九月丙午，以端明殿學士、左散騎常侍、權知開封府事王樸為尚書戶部侍郎，充樞密副使；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, day bingwu, the Duanming Hall academician, Left Regular Attendant, and acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture Wang Pu was made Vice Minister of Revenue in the Ministry and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingwu, Wang Pu was made Vice Minister of Revenue and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 以右羽林統軍焦繼勛為左屯衛上將軍；

translations.literal: the Commander of the Right Feathered Forest Army Jiao Jixun was made General of the Left Garrison Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Jixun of the Right Feathered Forest was made general of the Left Garrison Guard;

sentences.zh: 以左衛上將軍楊承信為右羽林統軍；

translations.literal: the General of the Left Guard Yang Chengxin was made Commander of the Right Feathered Forest Army;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chengxin of the Left Guard was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest Army;

sentences.zh: 以左監門上將軍宋延渥為右神武統軍。

translations.literal: the General of the Left Gate Guards Song Yanwo was made Commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yanwo of the Left Gate Guards was made commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛酉，葬宣懿皇后於懿陵。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, day xinyou, the Empress Xuanyi was buried at Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on xinyou, Empress Xuanyi was buried at Yiling.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以右神武統軍宋延渥為廬州行營副部署。

translations.literal: On day guihai, the Commander of the Right Divine Martial Army Song Yanwo was made deputy commander of the Luzhou campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Song Yanwo, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was appointed deputy commander of the Luzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，舒州刺史郭令圖責授虢州教練使，坐棄郡逃歸也。

translations.literal: On day yichou, the prefect of Shuzhou Guo Lingtu was demoted and appointed drill commissioner of Guozhou for abandoning his commandery and fleeing back.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Shuzhou prefect Guo Lingtu was demoted to drill commissioner at Guozhou for abandoning his post and fleeing home.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「諸司職員皆系奏補，當執役之際，悉藉公勤，及聽選之時，尤資幹敏，茍非慎擇，漸致因循。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, an edict stated: "Staff of all offices are appointed by memorial. When performing duties they all rely on public diligence; when awaiting selection, keen competence is especially required. If selection is not careful, gradual laxity will follow.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin an edict declared that all office staff were appointed by memorial and must serve diligently; careless selection would breed slackness.

sentences.zh: 應諸司寺監，今後收補役人，並須人材俊利，身言可采，書劄堪中，自前行止，委無訛濫，勒本司關送吏部，引驗人材，考校筆劄。

translations.literal: All directorates and supervisorates, when hereafter recruiting service personnel, must all require talented and sharp men whose person and speech are acceptable and whose documents pass muster, whose prior conduct is truly without fraud, and compel their office to forward them to the Ministry of Personnel for verification of talent and examination of documents.
translations.idiomatic: All agencies recruiting clerks must choose able men of good character and competent writing, verify their records, and send them to the Ministry of Personnel for examination.

sentences.zh: 其中選者，連所試書跡及正身引過中書，余從前後格敕處分，仍每年只得一度奏補。」

translations.literal: Those selected among them, together with their trial handwriting and in person, were to be led past the Secretariat; the rest followed prior regulations and edicts. Each year only one round of memorial appointments was permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Successful candidates were to present their writing and appear before the Secretariat; appointments were limited to once per year under existing regulations."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，宣懿皇后神主入廟，時有司請為後立別廟，禮也。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, the spirit tablet of Empress Xuanyi entered the temple. At that time the relevant offices requested establishing a separate temple for the empress—this was ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Empress Xuanyi's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple; the court also proposed a separate temple for her, as ritual required.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔：「漳河以北郡縣，並許鹽貨通商，逐處有鹼鹵之地，一任人戶煎煉。」

translations.literal: On day jisi, an edict stated: "In all prefectures and counties north of the Zhang River, salt goods may be traded freely. Wherever there is alkaline brine, households are permitted to boil and refine salt."
translations.idiomatic: On jisi an edict permitted salt trade in all counties north of the Zhang River and allowed households to boil salt wherever brine was found."

sentences.zh: 壬申，以武平軍節度副使、知潭州軍府事宇文瓊為武清軍節度使，知潭州軍府事。

translations.literal: On day renshen, the deputy military governor of Wuping Army and administrator of Tanzhou military affairs Yuwen Qiong was made military governor of Wuqing Army and administrator of Tanzhou military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Yuwen Qiong was made Wuqing governor while continuing to administer Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，淮南招討使李重進奏，破淮賊於盛唐，斬二千級。

translations.literal: On day guiyou, the Huainan campaign commander Li Chongjin memorialized that he had defeated Huainan rebels at Sheng Tang and taken two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Li Chongjin reported defeating Huainan rebels at Sheng Tang with two thousand enemy killed.

sentences.zh: 太子賓客致仕薛仁謙卒。

translations.literal: The retired Crown Prince's Mentor Xue Renqian died.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Renqian, retired mentor to the Crown Prince, died.

sentences.zh: 丙子，襄州節度使、守太尉、兼中書令、陳王安審琦加守太師。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, the military governor of Xiangzhou, Guardian Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Chen Wang Shenqi was further made Guardian Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Wang Shenqi, Prince of Chen and governor of Xiangzhou, was promoted to Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 審琦鎮漢上十餘年，至是來朝，故以命寵之。

translations.literal: Shenqi had governed the Han River region for more than ten years; he now came to court, and therefore this appointment honored him.
