translations.idiomatic: Shenqi had governed the Han region for over ten years; this promotion honored his visit to court.

sentences.zh: 癸未，右拾遺趙守微杖一百，配沙門島。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, the Right Reminder Zhao Shouwei received one hundred strokes of the staff and was banished to Shamen Island.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Reminder Zhao Shouwei was flogged a hundred times and exiled to Shamen Island.

sentences.zh: 守微本村民也，形貌樸野，粗學為文。

translations.literal: Shouwei was originally a village man, plain and rustic in appearance, with rough learning in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwei was a rustic villager of plain appearance with only rudimentary literary training.

sentences.zh: 前年徒步上書，帝以急於取士，授右拾遺，聞者駭其事。

translations.literal: The year before last he walked on foot to submit a memorial. The Emperor, eager to recruit talent, appointed him Right Reminder; those who heard were astonished at the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Two years earlier he had walked to the capital with a memorial; the Emperor, eager for talent, made him Reminder—to general astonishment.

sentences.zh: 至是為妻父所訟，彰其醜行，故逐之。

translations.literal: At this time he was sued by his father-in-law, exposing his shameful conduct; therefore he was expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Now his father-in-law sued him, exposing scandalous conduct, and he was driven out.

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略·張昭傳》云：世宗好拔奇取俊，有自布衣上書、下僚言事者，多不次進用。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Zhang Zhao in Outline History of the Eastern Capital: Shizong loved to elevate the extraordinary and select the outstanding. Those who submitted memorials as commoners or spoke on affairs as junior officials were often promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: (The Outline History of the Eastern Capital records that Shizong favored promoting unusual talent; commoners and junior officials who petitioned were often advanced out of turn.

sentences.zh: 昭諫曰：「昔唐初劉洎、馬周起徒步，太宗擢用為相，其後朱樸、柳璨在下僚，昭宗亦以大用，然則太宗用之於前而國興，昭宗用於後而國亡，士之難知也如此。

translations.literal: Zhao remonstrated: "In early Tang, Liu Ji and Ma Zhou rose from foot soldiers; Taizong promoted them to chancellor. Later Zhu Pu and Liu Can were junior officials whom Zhaozong also greatly employed. Yet Taizong used men in the former case and the state flourished; Zhaozong used men in the latter case and the state perished. How difficult it is to know gentlemen is shown thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao warned: "In early Tang, Liu Ji and Ma Zhou rose from obscurity and Taizong made them chancellors—the state prospered. Later Zhu Pu and Liu Can were promoted by Zhaozong—and the state fell. Talent is hard to judge.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下存舊法而用人，以劉、馬為鑒，朱、柳為戒，則善矣。」）〉

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to preserve the old methods in employing men, taking Liu and Ma as mirrors and Zhu and Liu as warnings—then it would be good." )〉
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to follow established methods, taking Liu and Ma as models and Zhu and Liu as warnings." )〉

sentences.zh: 甲申，宣授今上同州節度使兼殿前都指揮使，宣授內外馬步軍都軍頭袁彥為曹州節度使兼侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, Zhao Kuangyin was announced and appointed military governor of Tongzhou and Commander of the Palace Front Army; Yuan Yan, head of all inner and outer horse and foot armies, was announced and appointed military governor of Caozhou and Commander of the Palace Foot Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Zhao Kuangyin was appointed Tongzhou governor and palace front army commander; Yuan Yan was made Caozhou governor and commander of the palace foot army.

sentences.zh: 戊子，右神武統軍張彥超卒。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, the Commander of the Right Divine Martial Army Zhang Yanchao died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Zhang Yanchao, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, died.

sentences.zh: 十一月己丑朔，詔廢天下無名祠廟。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, day jichou, an edict abolished all unlicensed shrines throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month an edict abolished unauthorized shrines throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 庚子，日南至，帝不受朝賀，以宣懿皇后遷祔日近也。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, the winter solstice, the Emperor did not accept court congratulations because the day for transferring Empress Xuanyi's tablet to joint worship was near.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the winter solstice, the Emperor declined New Year congratulations because Empress Xuanyi's enshrinement was imminent.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，江南進奉使孫晟下獄死，江南進奉使鐘謨責授耀州司馬。

translations.literal: On day yisi, the Jiangnan tribute envoy Sun Sheng died in prison; the Jiangnan tribute envoy Zhong Mo was demoted and appointed military assistant of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Jiangnan envoy Sun Sheng died in prison; envoy Zhong Mo was demoted to military assistant at Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，放華山隱者陳摶歸山。

translations.literal: On day wushen, the Huashan recluse Chen Tuan was released to return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Huashan recluse Chen Tuan was released to return to his mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 帝素聞摶有道術，征之赴闕，月餘放還舊隱。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long heard that Tuan possessed the Way and arts; he summoned him to court and after more than a month released him to his former seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had heard of Chen Tuan's mystical arts, summoned him to court, and after a month sent him back to seclusion.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，殿前都指揮使張永德奏，敗濠州送糧軍二千人於下蔡，奪米船十餘艘。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, the Commander of the Palace Front Army Zhang Yongde memorialized that he had defeated two thousand grain-transport troops from Hao Prefecture at Xiacai and seized more than ten rice boats.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Zhang Yongde reported defeating two thousand Hao grain convoy troops at Xiacai and capturing over ten supply boats.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李穀以風痹請告十旬，三上表求解所任，不允。

translations.literal: The chief minister Li Gu requested leave for ten-day leave because of wind paralysis and three times submitted memorials asking to be relieved of his post; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Gu requested three months' leave for rheumatism and thrice asked to resign; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月己未朔，以給事中張鑄為光祿卿，鑄訴以官名與祖諱同，尋改秘書監，判光祿寺事。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, day jiwei, the Supervising Secretary Zhang Zhu was made Director of the Imperial Banquets. Zhu pleaded that the office title shared a character with his ancestor's taboo name; he was soon changed to Director of the Secretariat and administered affairs of the Imperial Banquets directorate.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month Zhang Zhu was made Director of Imperial Banquets but pleaded that the title violated his ancestor's taboo; he was reassigned as Secretariat director overseeing the Banquets office.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以許州節度使韓通兼侍衛馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, the military governor of Xuzhou Han Tong was made concurrent Chief Commandant of the Palace Horse and Foot Armies.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Xuzhou governor Han Tong was also made chief commandant of the palace horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以右領軍大將軍、權判三司張美領三司使。

translations.literal: On day renxu, the General of the Right Army Guards and acting administrator of the Three Departments Zhang Mei was placed in charge as Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Zhang Mei, acting head of the Three Departments, was appointed their commissioner.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以滑州節度使兼殿前都指揮使、駙馬都尉張永德為殿前都點校。

translations.literal: On day renshen, the military governor of Huazhou, Commander of the Palace Front Army, and Commander of the Imperial Sons-in-Law Zhang Yongde was made overall inspector of the palace front army.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Zhang Yongde, Huazhou governor and palace commander, was made overall inspector of the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 發陳、蔡、宋、亳、潁、曹、單等州丁夫城下蔡。

translations.literal: Corvée laborers were mobilized from Chen, Cai, Song, Bo, Ying, Cao, Shan, and other prefectures to fortify Xiacai.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers from Chen, Cai, Song, Bo, Ying, Cao, Shan, and neighboring prefectures were drafted to fortify Xiacai.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，故襄邑令劉居方贈右補闕，男士衡賜學究出身，獎廉吏也。

translations.literal: On day xinsi, the former magistrate of Xiangyi Liu Jufang was posthumously given the title of Right Supplementation Censor; the gentleman Shi Heng was granted the status of classical scholar graduate—to reward upright officials.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the late magistrate Liu Jufang was posthumously made Right Supplementation Censor and Shi Heng was granted scholar status, rewarding honest officials.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔兵部尚書張昭纂修太祖實錄及梁均王、唐清泰帝兩朝實錄。

translations.literal: On day guihai, an edict ordered the Minister of War Zhang Zhao to compile and revise the Veritable Records of Taizu and the veritable records of the two reigns of the Liang Prince of Jun and Tang Emperor Qingtai.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Minister of War Zhang Zhao was ordered to compile the Veritable Records of Taizu and the records of the Liang and Tang Qingtai reigns.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：同修撰官委張昭定名奏請，至四年正月，張昭奏請國子祭酒尹拙、太子詹事劉溫叟同編修。）〉

translations.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties states: Co-compilers were to be named by Zhang Zhao in a memorial. By the first month of the fourth year, Zhang Zhao memorialized requesting the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Yin Zhuo and the Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Liu Wensou to join in compilation.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties records that Zhang Zhao was to nominate co-compilers; in the first month of the fourth year he proposed Yin Zhuo and Liu Wensou join the project.)〉

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「史館所少書籍，宜令本館諸處求訪補填。

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Books lacking in the History Office should be sought and supplemented everywhere by that office.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered the History Office to seek out missing books everywhere.

sentences.zh: 如有收得書籍之家，並許進書人據部帙多少等第，各與恩澤，如是卷帙少者，量給資帛。

translations.literal: If any household had obtained books, donors were permitted to present books according to the number of fascicles in graded ranks, each receiving favors; if fascicles were few, stipends in goods and silks were given in measure.
translations.idiomatic: Households presenting books would receive rewards graded by the number of volumes; smaller donations would receive proportionate gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 如館內已有之書，不在進納之限。

translations.literal: Books already held within the office were not within the limit for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Duplicates of books already in the collection were not eligible for rewards.

sentences.zh: 仍委中書門下，於朝官內選差三十人，據見在書籍，各求真本校勘，署校官姓名，逐月具功課申報中書門下。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat was further entrusted to select thirty men from among court officials, who according to existing books would each seek true texts for collation, sign the collators' names, and each month report their work achievements to the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was to select thirty court officials to collate existing texts, sign their work, and report monthly to the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 戊子，淮南道招討使李重進奏，破淮賊二千人於塌山北。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, the Huainan campaign commander Li Chongjin memorialized that he had defeated two thousand Huainan rebels north of Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Li Chongjin reported defeating two thousand Huainan rebels north of Tashan.
